doc.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Scale, residuals and the fun of the studio era
summary: Scale was around $40-50 an hour, with residuals paid after ten weeks, which musicians spent at the bar.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well I can’t remember exactly. I think it ran, it might have run anywhere from $40 to $50 for the hour or something like that, then the overtime. So if you went in for a couple of hours, it could be $100 or $75. Those things kept — and they had residuals to them as well. If they were used over a ten week period or something like that why there would be another part. So you’d go in to the union after ten weeks or some time, you’d be apt to find repayments on some of these — you know, cigarette commercials and things like that that were going on then. And as I told you you would just run to Jim & Andy’s with all those immediately. That was like found money. Lots of nice drinks.
Productive time for music in New York, for musicians anyway.
Yeah it was exciting. The guys were all full of fun I think and hung together. A good lot really.
